decision_question: How can yt3 reduce avoidable time to trustworthy change feedback without weakening the checks that protect main?

sources.title: Software Engineering at Google, Chapter 7: Measuring Engineering Productivity

goals.statement: Changes receive timely, interpretable CI feedback while existing safety checks stay intact.
goals.positive_action: Inspect slow CI stages and optimize without weakening the canonical validation gate.
goals.negative_action: Do not infer that green Actions alone proves quality; preserve the current gate and investigate flaky results.

signals.statement: A pull request receives an actionable CI workflow result early enough to inform review.
The first CI workflow attempt returns an explicit outcome that supports failure triage.

metrics.name: CI workflow p95 elapsed time
metrics.definition: The 95th-percentile elapsed time from a pull-request CI workflow run being created to its completed result.
metrics.formula: p95(updated_at - created_at) for completed pull_request CI workflow runs with run_attempt = 1
metrics.aggregation: Nearest-rank p95; n=88; median=124 seconds; max=452 seconds
limitations: The run timestamps are a proxy for time to feedback and can include queue and service-update delay.
The CI workflow is not configured as a required branch-protection status check in the observed repository state.
CI duration is not a measurement of developer focus, total engineering effort, or software quality.
A low sample count or changes in runner capacity can make comparisons misleading.

metrics.name: CI workflow-run success rate (run_attempt = 1)
metrics.definition: The proportion of completed pull-request CI workflow runs whose GitHub Actions run_attempt is 1 and whose conclusion is success. This counts workflow runs, not distinct pull requests; one pull request can contribute multiple runs.
metrics.formula: 100 * successful completed first-attempt pull_request CI workflow runs / all completed first-attempt pull_request CI workflow runs
metrics.aggregation: 63 successful / 88 completed workflow runs with run_attempt=1 = 71.6%; multiple runs from one pull request can be counted; report numerator and denominator
limitations: A green CI run is not proof that a change is defect-free.
The unit is a workflow run, not a distinct pull request; multiple commits on one PR can create multiple run_attempt=1 records.
This CI workflow is not configured as a required branch-protection status check in the observed repository state.
Cancelled, skipped, and infrastructure-failure conclusions must be reported separately rather than silently counted as success or failure.
A pass-rate change is descriptive and does not establish that a particular process change caused it.

anti_patterns: Do not treat lines of code or commit counts as productivity outcomes.
Do not optimize a convenient metric before stating the decision and desired outcome.
Do not claim that green CI proves code quality or that a single before/after change establishes causality.
